issue.title: Add Cloudflare to Flask Hosting Platforms docs?
issue.author: hoodmane

summary.text: This open issue requests adding Cloudflare’s Flask deployment guide to the Hosting Platforms documentation. The guide’s initially missing example was reportedly added, but the remaining question is whether linking provider-authored documentation is appropriate given concerns about advertising. No final acceptance or rejection is recorded.

known_facts.text: The reporter says Cloudflare Workers supports Flask applications and asks for a link to Cloudflare’s short deployment guide from Flask’s Hosting Platforms section.
A maintainer observed that the examples repository linked by the guide did not include the referenced example; the reporter subsequently said it had been merged and was available.
The reporter later requested a yes, no, or conditional response to the proposal.

A maintainer said similar company-authored additions had historically been declined as potentially advertising, while also noting that Cloudflare is comparable in scale to providers already listed and might therefore be acceptable.
The maintainer pointed to the Pallets donation page but explicitly made no promise of service in exchange for a donation.
Two repository searches using “Cloudflare hosting” and “hosting platforms” found no eligible candidate issues beyond the target.

missing_information: What neutral, non-promotional wording and selection criterion should govern this link and comparable provider links?
Is the maintainer willing to review a narrowly scoped documentation PR, or is a broader hosting-platform listing policy needed first?
content.draft_reply: Thanks for adding the missing example and for following up. The remaining concern is not whether Cloudflare can host Flask, but whether linking provider-authored guides from this page amounts to advertising and how we would apply the same standard consistently to other providers. Cloudflare’s scale relative to the services already listed weighs in favor of considering it, but this is not yet a firm approval. A useful next step would be a narrowly scoped documentation PR with neutral wording and no marketing claims, together with a brief explanation of the general criterion under which Cloudflare—and comparable providers—should qualify. Would you be willing to propose that wording and criterion?
limitations: The Cloudflare guide, its example repository, Flask’s current documentation, source code, and release history were not independently inspected; statements about them are attributed to the issue participants.
The recorded searches found no eligible comparison candidates, but keyword searches cannot establish that no duplicate or related issue exists.

The label catalog was complete as returned, but several labels—including the recommended ones—had no descriptions, so their applicability was inferred cautiously from their names and the issue’s content.

sources.title: Add Cloudflare to Flask Hosting Platforms docs?
sources.excerpt:
Cloudflare workers supports deploying Flask applications. We have the following short guide for deploying Flask workers:
https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/languages/python/packages/flask/

Could we add a link to this page to the "Hosting Platforms" section of the docs?

sources.title: Comment by hoodmane
Comment by davidism
sources.excerpt:
Author association: MEMBER
Created: 2026-10-30T15:11:16Z

Sorry for the delay. I'm a bit conflicted. Historically, I've declined PRs from various companies to add their docs to this list. It feels like advertising. I'm not prepared to name a donation (recurring?) amount that will cover it. Cloudflare is absolutely at the same scale as the others listed here, so I guess it's acceptable in that sense.

With no promise of any particular service, I'll point you to our donate page: https://palletsprojects.com/donate. I'd hope Cloudflare would be interested in donating to Flask regardless of a link.
